SINAVE dataset

Source: vignettes/sinave_dataset.Rmd
sinave_dataset.Rmd

Versión en español

Introduction

The National Epidemiological Surveillance System (SINAVE) of the Ministry of Health of Mexico has 11 datasets of vector-borne diseases: RICKETT, CHAGAS, FIEBRE_NILO, LEISHMAN, ENCEFALITIS, FIEBREMAYARO, FIEBREAMARILLA, PALUDISMO, ZIKA, CHIKUNGUNYA and DENGUE. Their use is restricted to the staff of the Ministry of Health (state and federal), in particular the departments of Epidemiology and of Vector-Borne Diseases.

The temporal resolution of the datasets is daily and the spatial resolution is the house, so they can be aggregated by neighbourhood, locality, municipality and state to make tables, graphs and maps.

In the dengueverse the datasets are loaded into R with two densnv functions:

  1. read(): reads one or several txt files of a folder.
  2. read_dengue_dataset(): reads the dengue dataset and filters it by geographic level and case status.

The boldenr package is being replaced by densnv; these two functions are recommended.

library(densnv)
path     <- "dge/denv/2026"                  # folder with the txt files
path_txt <- "dge/denv/2026/DENGUE2_.txt"     # dengue file

Main columns

column content
ANO, SEM Year and epidemiological week
FEC_INI_SIGNOS_SINT Date of onset of symptoms
ESTATUS_CASO 1 probable, 2 confirmed, 3 discarded
CVE_EDO_RES, CVE_MPO_RES, CVE_LOC_RES State, municipality and locality of residence (INEGI keys)
CVE_EDO_REP, CVE_MPO_REP, CVE_LOC_REP State, municipality and locality of report (INEGI keys)
DES_DIAG_FINAL Final diagnosis: non-severe dengue, with warning signs or severe
IDE_EDA_ANO, IDE_SEX Age (years) and sex

In non-endemic areas the positive cases are reported in the place where they were exposed, so the place of report (*_REP) is the place of transmission. In endemic areas report and residence are almost the same.

read()

argument value definition
path string Path of the folder with the txt files
vbd string Disease of interest (RICKETT, CHAGAS, FIEBRE_NILO, LEISHMAN, ENCEFALITIS, FIEBREMAYARO, FIEBREAMARILLA, PALUDISMO, ZIKA, CHIKUNGUNYA or DENGUE)
complete logical TRUE for the arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya and Zika); FALSE for the other diseases 
read(path = path, vbd = "DENGUE", complete = TRUE) |>
  dim()
#> [1] 81352   432
read(path = path, vbd = "DENGUE", complete = FALSE) |>
  dim()
#> [1] 81352    34

A summary of the dataset, without showing rows:

read(path = path, vbd = "DENGUE", complete = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c("ANO", "SEM", "ESTATUS_CASO", "IDE_EDA_ANO",
                                "IDE_SEX", "DES_DIAG_FINAL"))) |>

read_dengue_dataset()

argument value definition
path string Path of the dengue txt file
spatial_resolution string Geographic level: “country”, “state” or “municipality”
status_caso integer Case status: 1 probable, 2 confirmed, 3 discarded (one or several)
des_edo_res string State of residence, in uppercase (for “state” and “municipality”)
des_mpo_res string Municipality of residence, in uppercase (for “municipality”)

Country 

x <- read_dengue_dataset(path = path_txt,
                         spatial_resolution = "country",
                         status_caso = c(1, 2, 3))
dim(x)
#> [1] 81346    35
table(x$ESTATUS_CASO)
#> 
#>     1     2     3 
#> 41470 10870 29006

Another way to read the dataset

To use the whole dataset, without filters, with the other densnv functions (plt_pyramid(), mp_animated_mpo(), rt_dengue()…):

x <- data.table::fread("DENGUE2_.txt", quote = "", fill = TRUE)

The arguments quote = "" and fill = TRUE avoid errors with the quotes and incomplete rows of the SINAVE files.

Confidentiality

The datasets contain addresses and personal data. Individual rows must not be shared or published; reports, presentations and repositories should show only aggregated counts.
